basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 11:29 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 153. Quomodo intelligendum est quod dicitur: Pater Melchae ipse est Pater Jeschae'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 153. Quomodo intelligendum est quod dicitur: Pater Melchae ipse est Pater Jeschae (Gen. XI, 29). Vel qui [ Ms., quae] fuit Jescha?-- Resp. Thare genuit Abraham, Nachor et Aran: Aran vero genuit Lot, et Melcham et Sarri, cognomento Jescham, et acceperunt uxores, Abraham Sarri, Nachor vero Melcham. Necdum autem inter patruos et fratrum filios nuptiae lege prohibitae fuerant.
